findings.title: Constructor null-check tests grantType instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: AccessTokenContext's constructor is supposed to reject a null raw token id, but the second requireNonNull call checks grantType again (message says 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'). A null rawTokenId is stored. encodeTokenId then concatenates ':' with that value, and Java string conversion turns null into the literal 'null', so every such token gets the same jti suffix (for example onrtac:null). Distinct access tokens would share a JWT ID, which breaks uniqueness for revocation, replay detection, and event correlation. The current TokenManager caller passes KeycloakModelUtils.generateId(), so this is latent, but the constructor is the shared entry point for the new SPI and does not enforce the invariant it claims to enforce.

findings.title: Access-token ID matcher checks the wrong characters and inverts the match
findings.body: isAccessTokenId is now what expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, and expectAuthReqIdToToken use for Details.TOKEN_ID. After splitting on ':', it treats items[0].substring(3, 5) as the grant shortcut and returns false (no match) when that slice equals the expected shortcut. Both parts are wrong. The wire format is 2-char session type, 2-char token type, 2-char grant type, so the grant is substring(4, 6): for onrtac the grant is ac, while substring(3, 5) is ta (last char of token type 'rt'/'lt' plus the first grant char). The equality test is also inverted, so a real match is rejected. For every built-in grant, substring(3, 5) is 't' plus the grant's first character, which is never the grant shortcut, so the check never fires and the matcher accepts any six-char prefix plus a UUID. These new assertions will not fail if authorization-code, refresh, device, or CIBA access tokens are encoded with the wrong grant (including the 'na' fallback). A prefix shorter than 5 characters throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of a failed assertion. The check should require a prefix of at least 6 characters and substring(4, 6) equal to the expected shortcut.

findings.title: New getShortcut() method has no default and aborts server startup
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is the extension point for custom grant types, and getShortcut() was added with no default implementation. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit walks every OAuth2GrantType factory and calls getShortcut() unconditionally. A custom grant JAR compiled against the previous interface does not have that method, so the call throws AbstractMethodError during provider startup and Keycloak fails to boot. A recompiled factory that returns null also aborts startup, because the shortcut is inserted into a ConcurrentHashMap, which rejects null keys. A default method is required so existing providers keep the server up, and postInit must reject invalid shortcuts with an explicit error instead of an NPE or AbstractMethodError.

findings.title: Grant shortcuts are not validated as 2-character unique codes
findings.body: Access-token ids are a fixed 6-character prefix (session type, token type, grant shortcut, 2 characters each) plus ':' plus the raw id. The decoder rejects any other prefix length. postInit stores each grant shortcut with no check that it is non-null, exactly 2 characters, free of ':', or unique beyond a map-size comparison. OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut's javadoc says shortcuts are 'usually like 3-letters', which cannot be represented in this format. A custom grant that follows that javadoc still passes the size check, and encodeTokenId will issue ids such as onrtabc:<uuid>. Decoding those ids throws IllegalArgumentException, so the context this feature exists to recover is unreadable. The hot-deploy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut (puts around lines 113 and 131) also overwrites grantsByShortcuts without re-checking length or uniqueness. Two grants that share a shortcut leave one decode mapping, so previously issued tokens of the overwritten grant are reported as the other grant type. Registration should reject anything other than a unique 2-character shortcut, and the javadoc must match that contract.

findings.title: Decoder throws on unknown prefixes instead of falling back like legacy ids
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId returns an UNKNOWN session type, token type, and grant when the jti has no ':'. If the id contains ':' but the prefix is not exactly 6 characters, or any 2-character slice is missing from the in-memory maps, it throws IllegalArgumentException. The length error says the token id 'Expected length of 6', but the check is only on the prefix before the colon, so the message is wrong and will mislead operators. Unknown shortcuts are a normal compatibility case, not corruption: feature-gated grants are absent from the maps when that feature is disabled or not deployed on this node (CIBA 'ci', device 'dg', token-exchange 'te', pre-authorized code 'pc'), and another Keycloak version can mint shortcuts this node does not know. Introspection or session lookup that uses this method, which is the stated purpose of the encoding, will then fail a still-valid access token instead of falling back to the old online-then-offline lookup. Unsupported prefixes should return an UNKNOWN context, the same as colon-less legacy ids.

findings.title: Non-standard token exchange issues access tokens with unknown grant
findings.body: The encoded grant type is whatever was stored on the client-session attribute Constants.GRANT_TYPE. If that attribute is missing, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider records 'na' (unknown). Token exchange does not go through OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, which is why this provider had to set the attribute itself before generateAccessToken(). Only StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient was updated. TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory still turns on legacy TOKEN_EXCHANGE, TOKEN_EXCHANGE_FEDERATED_V2, and TOKEN_EXCHANGE_SUBJECT_IMPERSONATION_V2, and those providers are not in this change. StandardTokenExchangeProvider rejects requested_subject, so impersonation cannot be this method. Those other flows still call TokenManager to mint access tokens, so their jti grant shortcut is 'na' rather than 'te'. Follow-up token-exchange logic that branches on the encoded grant (the #37117 case described in the PR) will not recognize them. The new AssertEvents matcher does not actually verify the grant shortcut, so CI will not catch this.

findings.title: Replacing form params leaves the cached grant type stale
findings.body: grantType is captured once in the Context constructor from formParams.getFirst(grant_type) and is what OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse writes into the client session before the access token id is encoded. setFormParams replaces formParams but does not recompute grantType, so getGrantType() can disagree with the params the grant then processes. A caller that uses the existing setter to change the request after construction will encode the original grant type into the access-token id. The constructor also now dereferences formParams, so a null map NPEs, which the previous constructor accepted. This change also removes the public Context(Context) copy constructor, so extensions that cloned a context that way no longer compile and have no other way to rebuild grantType.
